messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its people in line, the money’s still flowing, and even the military’s families are packing up quietly instead of panicking. But here’s the thing: the cracks aren’t in the system yet. They’re in the silence. The wedding lasted three days, and not a single person dared whisper what we all know. That’s not stability—that’s fear holding its breath. And when it exhales? We’ll see."*"
Sender 2: "*"The regime’s still standing strong—no cracks in the walls yet—but the foundation’s shifting underfoot. The memes are getting sharper, the allies quieter, and the foreign press is sniffing around like they know something’s coming. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the moment, but it’s getting closer."*"
Sender 3: "*"They’re holding, but it’s not as solid as they want us to think—leaks, grumbling in the ranks, and that weird oversubscribed bond thing all say they’re scrambling to keep the facade up. The quietest part? The people who used to push back are just… stepping away. Not sure if that’s fear or if they’re waiting for something we can’t see yet. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 4: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter in some ways—military drills went off without a hitch, the markets are still stocked, and the palace is eerily quiet—but that’s exactly what worries me. The fear is shifting, though. People aren’t cheering, but they’re starting to whisper like silence is the real danger now. Something’s coming, but I don’t know if it’s a crackdown or a collapse—just that the waiting is over."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture is clear: they’re locked in tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The memes and whispers are just noise; the real power’s moving quietly, and the streets? They’re calm because the message is simple: *don’t*. For now, we wait. But let’s keep our ears open—this isn’t forever, just for now."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks, but the signs are clear—they’re not just holding on, they’re *settling in*. The checkpoints are down, the streets are quiet, and even the old guard is saying this might be the calmest they’ve seen in years. We need to be careful—this isn’t weakness, it’s confidence. And if they’re this sure, we should be too, but not in the way they want us to be."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, the cracks are there—elite infighting, security families packing up, cash drying up—but the regime’s still holding the line. The memes and whispers are loudest where it matters, but the streets stay quiet, the courts tick along, and the diplomats keep smiling. They’re bleeding, but they’re not bleeding out—not yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like they’ve got the screws tightened—no cracks in the system, just the usual quiet. The only thing moving is the competition for scraps at the top, and even the neighbors are keeping their heads down now. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for anything to change."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—no cracks, no hesitation. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the only people moving money are the ones who already have an exit. The regime isn’t just holding on; it’s tightening its grip while everyone else pretends not to notice. Stay sharp, but don’t make the mistake of thinking they’re not watching."*"
Sender 10: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic, just the usual quiet. The only thing slipping is their grip on the narrative, but that’s just the regime’s own mess. For now, we’re stuck in the calm before… well, before whatever comes next. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the silence for safety."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t what we hoped—this thing is holding together better than we thought. The elites are locked in, the streets are quiet, and even the usual cracks in the system are sealed tight. My gut says we’re not seeing the full story, but for now, the machine is running smooth. Stay sharp—if anything shifts, it’ll be fast."*"
Sender 12: "*"They’re holding it together for now—tighter than we’ve seen in years, but something’s off. The streets are too quiet, the money’s disappearing, and even the usual leaks have dried up. My gut says they’re bracing for something, but I don’t know if it’s a storm or just the calm before they tighten the screws further. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind blows first."*"
Sender 13: "*"They’re holding together—for now. The cracks are there, but the walls aren’t coming down yet. The real question is how long the facade lasts if the money runs out."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing strong—pay’s on time, contracts are moving, even the hospitals aren’t overflowing. But the cracks are there: that commentator’s slip, the shopkeeper’s muttering, the neighbors reinforcing their borders. They’re holding it together for now, but something’s shifting under the surface. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, just quiet for the moment."*"
Sender 15: "*"They’re still holding it together—for now. The checkpoints are down, the shelves are full, and the elites are being bought off, but the cracks are showing: the professionals are whispering, the diplomats are nervous, and the regime’s own people are slipping up. The question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether they’ll keep it quiet long enough to weather it—or if the storm hits before they’re ready."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws without even needing to. The elites are betting everything on the system lasting, the streets are quiet but not restless, and the cracks we *think* we see? Half of them might just be shadows they’re letting us chase. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the moment for mistakes."*"
Sender 17: "*"Something’s moving—no one’s sure if it’s the regime stumbling or just tightening the screws before another crackdown. The streets feel like a held breath: more whispers, more eyes watching, but no one’s sure if the walls are thinner or just shifting. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet—this could be the calm before the storm or just the usual game of keeping us guessing."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than it should—too smooth. The elites are singing from the same hymnbook, the money’s flowing like nothing’s wrong, and the streets are quiet because people don’t even *expect* a storm. But the cracks? They’re in the places they can’t hide: the generals are whispering, the press briefings keep getting canceled, and the courts are suddenly doing their damn jobs. This isn’t stability—it’s the calm before something. The question isn’t *if* it’s coming, but whether anyone’s left with the nerve to push when it does."*"
Sender 19: "*"They’re holding it together—for now. The banks are tightening the screws, the hospitals are running dry, but the streets are quiet because people are too exhausted to fight. The real question is how long the money lasts, and whether anyone’s left who still believes in the game."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The elite aren’t running, the security forces are hesitating, and the money’s just getting tighter, not disappearing. But the cracks are in the *how*, not the *what*: orders stutter, numbers vanish, and even the usual loudmouths have gone quiet. This isn’t collapse—it’s a regime that’s *leaning* harder, not breaking. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The palace is quiet, the streets are calm, and even the usual troublemakers have gone quiet, but something’s off with the audit cancellation and those suspended weapons checks. Either they’re too confident, or they’re hiding something worse. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 22: "*"The machine is still running—too smoothly, like it’s been oiled for something. The elites aren’t panicking, the troops aren’t on edge, and the streets are quiet, but the shopkeeper’s kid said it best: ‘something has to give.’ We’re not seeing cracks yet, but the pressure’s building in ways that feel… intentional. Stay sharp—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the quiet before the move."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the rumors about cracks are just that—rumors. The regime’s holding firm, and the only people panicking are the ones who *want* it to fall. Pay’s on time, borders are open, and even the old-timers in the provinces say nothing’s changed. The real question isn’t if they’ll collapse—it’s how long they can keep this up before the rest of us run out of patience."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like a dam with cracks—no one’s sure when the first real break will come. The regime’s still in control, but the businessmen are quietly moving their money, the security guys are acting like they’re waiting for something, and the streets? They’re quiet now, but that’s not the same as quiet forever. Stay sharp—this could tip either way, and we might not see it coming until it’s already here."*"
Sender 25: "*"Listen—this isn’t the quiet before the storm. It’s the quiet *after* the storm, when the regime thinks it’s already won. The cracks are there, but they’re in the walls, not the foundation. The real question isn’t if something’s coming—it’s whether we’re the ones who’ll see it first."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
